Method of Attack: Authenticated attackers with basic user permissions can upload arbitrary files and remotely execute arbitrary code
Attackers logged in as subscribers or low-level users upload menu themes archived as ZIP files containing malicious PHP files
After archive extraction, attackers access files via site frontend to remotely execute malicious code leading to full site takeover
Vulnerabilities allow forging requests to modify plugin settings enabling arbitrary file upload and remote code execution
Impacted Systems: WordPress sites using Responsive Menu plugin versions 4.0.0 up to 4.0.3 or running in legacy mode
Attack Vector: Authenticated user upload of malicious ZIP archives containing PHP files via plugin theme upload function
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious PHP files in uploaded ZIP archives
Site frontend access to uploaded malicious files
